question: Should consecutive malformed `pullAudio` payloads consume the existing five-error budget and shut down the Google Meet bridge?
rationale: The implementation and proof establish the behavior, but only the owner of the existing resilience policy can decide whether malformed node output should be treated like repeated transport failure or skipped indefinitely.

options.title: Use the existing cutoff
options.body: Count malformed payloads as input failures, recover after isolated corruption, and close after five consecutive malformed chunks to avoid an unbounded broken bridge.

options.title: Drop malformed chunks indefinitely
options.body: Reject malformed audio without consuming the shutdown budget, favoring session availability at the cost of potentially endless warnings and a permanently silent bridge.

recommendation.title: Use the existing cutoff
recommendation.body: Count malformed payloads as input failures, recover after isolated corruption, and close after five consecutive malformed chunks to avoid an unbounded broken bridge.

likelyOwner.reason: BsnizND introduced the exact transient-recovery and five-consecutive-failure shutdown policy this PR extends.
